name: Kailasanathar Temple, Srivaikuntam
deity: Shiva as Kailasanathar — the shrine of Saturn (Shani) among the Nava Kailasam
period: A Shiva temple of the Nava Kailasam on the Tamiraparani, held in tradition to the lineage of Sage Agastya's disciple Uromacha Munivar
summary: At Srivaikuntam on the Tamiraparani — the same town as the Vishnu Divya Desam — Shiva stands as Kailasanathar, the Saturn shrine among the nine planetary Kailasam.

sections.history: Srivaikuntam, on the Tamiraparani a short way from Tirunelveli, holds a Kailasanathar temple among the Nava Kailasam, in the town also known for its Vishnu Divya Desam. It is one of the Nava Kailasam — the nine Shiva temples of the Tamiraparani, raised by tradition in the lineage of Sage Agastya and worshipped together as the planetary shrines of the Shaivas. Among the Nava Kailasam it is honoured as the shrine of Saturn, Shani — sought by devotees for relief from the affliction of the slow planet.
sections.architecture: Built in the Dravidian manner of the Pandya country and its later patrons, the temple is entered through a gateway tower and gathered around the sanctum of Shiva as Kailasanathar, the lord of Kailasa, with the Goddess in her own shrine. Here the lord is worshipped as Kailasanathar. Pillared halls open before the sanctum, in the temple manner of the deep south.
sections.legends: The Nava Kailasam are worshipped together as the nine planetary Kailasam of the Shaivas: it is told that Sage Agastya set nine flowers upon the Tamiraparani and bade his disciple Uromacha Munivar raise a shrine of Kailasanathar wherever each flower came to rest, so that the nine planets are honoured across nine abodes of Shiva on one river. At Srivaikuntam the planet is Saturn, Shani, and the shrine is much sought by those who seek the grace of the slow planet.
sections.festivals: The temple keeps the Shaiva festivals — Maha Shivaratri, the offerings of the month of Margazhi, and the days of its planetary lord — with abhishekam and processions along the riverside. Devotees seeking relief from planetary affliction come to the shrine of their star among the nine.
sections.experience: A quiet riverside Kailasam among the nine, rewarding for the pilgrim who follows the Tamiraparani from one shrine to the next. As the Kailasam of Saturn, it takes its place in the single pilgrimage of the Nava Kailasam that gathers the nine planets into the abodes of Shiva.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan sessions and a midday closure; Maha Shivaratri and the planetary-lord days are busiest. Confirm current timings before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: It lies in the Tirunelveli–Thoothukudi country on the Tamiraparani, reachable by road from Tirunelveli; the nine Kailasam villages are strung along the river and are often taken together as a single pilgrimage.
